categories.main_business_segments: Sajo Seafood Co., Ltd. operates primarily in four segments: processed seafood distribution focusing on sashimi-grade tuna, general seafood distribution, food products mainly seaweed (kim), and distant-water fishing. The company also engages in storage and leasing businesses related to cold storage facilities. Their core operations include tuna processing and distribution, seaweed production and sales, and offshore fishing activities.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes advanced ultra-low temperature freezing technology (-60°C) for preserving sashimi-grade tuna to maintain freshness. It operates hygienic processing facilities compliant with HACCP standards, especially for seaweed products. In distant-water fishing, it employs longline and purse seine fishing methods with modern fishing vessels equipped with scientific data analysis for efficient operations.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include domestic and international seafood distributors, sushi restaurants, large retail chains like E-Mart and Homeplus, and overseas buyers primarily in Japan, Europe, North America, and Southeast Asia. The seaweed products target both domestic consumers and export markets such as China. The distant-water fishing segment supplies tuna to processing companies and export markets, mainly Japan and the US.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates mainly in South Korea with significant export activities to Japan, Europe, North America, Southeast Asia, and China. Its fishing vessels operate in the Pacific and Indian Oceans. Domestic operations include processing plants and distribution centers primarily in Seoul and Busan.
categories.supply_chain_position: Sajo Seafood operates across multiple points in the supply chain: upstream in distant-water fishing (raw material procurement), midstream in seafood processing and packaging, and downstream in distribution and retail sales. It controls raw material sourcing through its own fishing operations and maintains cold storage and processing facilities to ensure product quality.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company focuses on securing stable raw material supply amid global fishery resource restrictions, expanding export markets beyond Japan to Europe and Southeast Asia, and diversifying sales channels including e-commerce. It invests in product development for seaweed snacks and seasoning products and emphasizes HACCP certification and food safety. Operational efficiency improvements in fishing and processing, including fuel-saving technologies, are also strategic priorities.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through product sales of processed sashimi-grade tuna, general seafood, seaweed products, and canned tuna from distant-water fishing. Additional income comes from leasing cold storage facilities and related services. Export sales constitute a significant portion, especially to Japan and other overseas markets.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other large Korean seafood companies such as Dongwon Industries, Dongwon Fisheries, and Silla Trading. Sajo Seafood holds a competitive position due to its integrated supply chain from fishing to processing and strong relationships with Japanese buyers. The company benefits from high entry barriers in tuna fishing quotas and advanced processing capabilities.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of 2023, the company reported revenues of approximately 176 billion KRW, with a total asset base of about 320 billion KRW. The company experienced a revenue decline compared to the previous year but maintains a strong asset position. It operates multiple fishing vessels and processing facilities with steady production capacity. The company is classified as a mid-sized enterprise in Korea.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Sajo Seafood emphasizes its stable raw material procurement through ownership of fishing vessels and quota rights, ensuring consistent supply of high-quality sashimi-grade tuna. Its ultra-low temperature freezing and HACCP-certified processing facilities guarantee product freshness and safety. Strong partnerships with major Japanese trading companies and diversified sales channels, including e-commerce, differentiate it in the competitive seafood market.
